question: What should I do in the first hour if a permanent tooth gets knocked out?
reference_answer: A knocked-out permanent tooth is a time-critical emergency (ESC-03) with a 30–60 minute window for saving the tooth: (1) Pick up the tooth by the white crown only—never touch, scrub, or wipe the root; (2) If dirty, rinse gently for no more than 10 seconds in cold milk or sterile normal saline (never tap water, soap, or tissue); (3) If you are an alert, calm adult, gently reinsert it into the socket in the right orientation and bite softly on a clean handkerchief—otherwise store it submerged in cold pasteurized milk, sterile saline, or inside your cheek pouch (never dry or in tap water); and (4) Travel immediately to BrightSmile Dental Care during clinic hours (Mon–Sat, 09:30 AM – 08:30 PM, calling +91-20-5550-0140 en route for WLK-T1 trauma care) or go to a hospital dental emergency department if it is Sunday or after hours.
